Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/breach-candy/

**Q: What does our building need to do so the tutor can get in every week?**

A: Arrange a standing weekly clearance rather than a one-off visitor pass. Give security the tutor's name and mobile number once, with the day and the time window, and ask for it to be recorded as a recurring entry. This takes one conversation and saves about five minutes of friction every single week, which matters more than it sounds when a tutor has a second family to reach afterwards. If your building requires photo identification at the gate, tell the tutor in advance so they carry it. If visitor parking is possible, confirm it early, because parking is the most common reason a South Mumbai tutor asks to move a slot.

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/breach-candy/

**Q: Do we need a parent at home during the session?**

A: For a child up to roughly Year 8, yes, an adult should be at home, though not in the room. For older students it is not necessary and often counterproductive, because a fifteen-year-old will not admit confusion in front of a parent. What we do ask of every family is a parent available for five minutes at the end of the first session and at session four. Those two conversations are where the useful information passes. Many Breach Candy families use a working arrangement where staff are present and the parent takes a short call afterwards, which works perfectly well provided the tutor knows who to report to.

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/breach-candy/

**Q: Our child is in DP1 at Bombay International School and cannot decide which subject to take at Higher Level. Can a tutor help with that?**

A: Yes, and this is one of the most valuable things a tutor does in the first term of DP1. The decision is not about which subject the child enjoys this month. It turns on what the Higher Level syllabus actually adds in topics and paper length, what the internal assessment demands in that subject, what the intended university course requires, and honestly how the child performs under long-paper conditions rather than in class. A tutor who has taught both levels can describe the difference concretely instead of abstractly. Bring the school's subject outlines to the session. IB Gram is independent and not affiliated with the school.

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/breach-candy/

**Q: Is searching for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Breach Candy the right way to choose?**

A: It is the wrong question, honestly stated. There is no single strongest tutor, only the right fit between a specific student, a specific subject at a specific level, and an evening slot that will survive a full term. A superb Higher Level Chemistry teacher is the wrong choice for a Year 9 student who has lost confidence in Mathematics. A patient, well-organised generalist is often better value across three subjects than three specialists. Ask instead: has this person taught this board at this level, can they describe what my child cannot yet do, and will they still be arriving in November?

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/breach-candy/

**Q: What if we miss a session because of school events, travel or illness?**

A: Tell the tutor as early as you can, because a home visit cancelled on the afternoon has already cost them the evening, particularly if yours was the second lesson of a paired trip. Most tutors will reschedule within the same week where their timetable allows, and many will offer a shorter online session instead, which is often the better outcome during examination weeks. Repeated late cancellations are the most common reason a tutor gives up a slot, so if your family calendar is genuinely unpredictable, say so at the start and we will match you with someone whose week has slack in it.

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/breach-candy/

**Q: Can one tutor cover several subjects, or do we need a different person for each?**

A: One tutor can often cover several, and up to IGCSE that is usually the better arrangement. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is realistic at MYP and IGCSE level across, say, Mathematics, the Sciences and Economics, because the skills that are failing are frequently shared: reading the question, structuring an answer, showing method. At Diploma Programme Higher Level the picture changes and specialists earn their keep, particularly in Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and the languages. A sensible structure for a DP2 student is one specialist for the hardest Higher Level and one broader tutor for everything else.

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/breach-candy/

**Q: Will the tutor be travelling from the suburbs, and will Mumbai traffic make them late?**

A: No, and that is deliberate. Tutors for Breach Candy are matched within the island city rather than brought down from Andheri, Powai or Thane. A tutor facing an hour each way on the Western Express Highway will accept a booking in June and start asking to move it by August, which is worse for you than never having had them. South Mumbai has enough IB and IGCSE teaching experience in it that going north is rarely necessary. Within the island the real delays are the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak, which is why we ask for a window rather than an exact minute.

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/breach-candy/

**Q: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Byculla depend on?**

A: They depend on five things, and nobody can quote you a sensible figure without them: the board and level, how scarce the subject is, the teacher's experience with the exact component, the session length and frequency, and door-to-door travel time. A Diploma Programme Higher Level science costs more per hour than MYP Year 2 support because the pool of people who can teach it is smaller. Byculla has one genuine advantage here: a teacher coming in over the Eastern Freeway from Chembur or Wadala spends less of the evening on the road than one crossing from Worli, and travel time is part of what any rate covers. Ask for the rate, the session length and the cancellation rule in one message.

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/byculla/

**Q: Will a tutor really come to our home in Byculla on a weekday evening?**

A: Yes, and an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Byculla is easier to place on a weekday evening than one in most of South Mumbai. Byculla station is on the Central Line and the Eastern Freeway on-ramp is minutes away, so the evening shortlist includes teachers living in Wadala, Chembur and Ghatkopar alongside those in Parel and Mahalaxmi. The practical rules are the same as anywhere in the city: offer a slot after half past six rather than at five, keep it on the same weekday every week, and accept that heavy monsoon rain can turn a seven o'clock start into a quarter past. A fixed weekly slot survives a term. A floating one does not.

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/byculla/

**Q: We live in a tower overlooking Rani Baug. How does building and gate access work?**

A: Get the teacher onto the standing-entry list in the first week. In towers around Rani Baug, Piramal Aranya included, a weekly visitor pass means a queue at the desk and a lift wait at exactly the hour the session should be starting, while a registered weekly entry with a fixed day and time usually takes one conversation with the society office. Share the teacher's name, photo identity number and the arrival window. Tell them which lobby and which lift bank, because in a tall tower that is a real five minutes. If your building requires a resident to approve every visit, leave the gate a standing instruction in writing.

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/byculla/

**Q: Is a tutor travelling in over the Eastern Freeway reliable through the monsoon?**

A: Mostly yes, with one honest caveat. The Freeway is signal-free, so a Chembur or Wadala teacher has a predictable run into Byculla on a normal evening, which is why the eastern pool is usable here at all. It is also a single road: water at the Orange Gate end, or an incident on the Anik link, has no train substitute for that exact route. Ask any teacher travelling in what their fallback is before the term starts rather than during it. The two workable answers are the Harbour Line to Dockyard Road plus an auto, or moving that one session online and making up the contact time later in the week.

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/byculla/

**Q: My daughter is at Bombay International School and needs help in three subjects. One tutor or three?**

A: Two, usually. One teacher can carry two related subjects properly, typically a science with mathematics or two humanities. Three subjects across different groups means one of them gets the leftover energy of a long evening, and it is always the one the teacher knows least well. For a student at Bombay International School or JBCN International School, Parel, the better structure is a specialist for the subject that is actually failing, a second for the next one, and nothing at all for the third until the first two are stable. Three simultaneous standing slots also eat the evenings a teenager needs for their own revision.

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/byculla/

**Q: What makes the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Byculla for one child a poor fit for another?**

A: Component experience and pace, not credentials. The teacher who turns a disorganised DP2 student's Exploration around in three weeks is often too brisk for an anxious Year 9 who needs the same explanation twice without a sigh. A Cambridge IGCSE specialist who has never read an MYP task-specific clarification will struggle with a Year 8 at a school that marks on criteria. Ask about the exact paper, the exact criterion and the last student they took through it. Then watch one session. The fit you can see in ninety minutes is more reliable than any line on a profile, and the platform sends a different teacher if it is wrong.

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/byculla/

**Q: Does online tuition work as well as home classes for IGCSE?**

A: For a motivated Year 10 or 11, close to it. For a younger or distractible student, no. IB and IGCSE online tutoring in Byculla is genuinely better for scarce subjects, early-morning slots before a mock and the weeks when the roads are flooded, and sharing a past paper on screen with annotations works well. What online loses is the ability to watch a student's working as they write it, catch the moment they go quiet, and take the phone off the table. The common compromise in this corridor is one session at home each week for the hard subject plus one online session for review or a second subject.

Source: https://www.ibgram.com/mumbai/byculla/
